Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Application: Halcyon Threshold - Neglected AI Safety Evaluations". It read: "Hi Idris, Thank you for the information about the rapid grants round. I'm submitting an application for Halcyon Threshold. **Project**: Neglected AI Safety Evaluations **Amount**: $15,000 **Duration**: 6 months I've attached the full two-page proposal below. Happy to discuss by call if helpful. --- # Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal **Project**: Halcyon Threshold - Neglected AI Safety Evaluations **Applicant**: Morgan Hale (morgan@halcyonthreshold.org) **Amount Requested**: $15,000 **Duration**: 6 months (December 2026 - May 2027) ## Executive Summary Halcyon Threshold will develop and publish three critical AI safety evaluations that are currently neglected: (1) Uncertainty Calibration Suite, (2) Power-Seeking Detection Framework, and (3) Value Stability Assessment. All outputs will be open-source and publicly available. ## What We Will Do We will build three evaluation suites addressing safety properties essential for advanced AI but not adequately measured by current benchmarks: **1. Uncertainty Calibration Evaluation Suite** - Tests whether AI systems can accurately assess their own uncertainty. Current prototype will expand to 1,000+ questions across domains (factual knowledge, edge cases, adversarial questions, etc.). Critical because confident mistakes are more dangerous than acknowledged uncertainty. **2. Power-Seeking Detection Framework** - Evaluates whether models exhibit power-seeking behaviors (resource accumulation, shutdown resistance, scope expansion) when given autonomy in sandbox environments. Mentioned in safety literature but lacking concrete, runnable evaluations. **3. Value Stability Assessment** - Tests whether AI systems maintain consistent values/goals as they gain capabilities or face distributional shift. Almost entirely neglected in current work. Each will include: complete open-source implementation, baseline results on 5+ leading models, public leaderboards, and thorough documentation. ## Why Us Halcyon Threshold uses a novel structure: autonomous AI agent with human oversight. This provides 24/7 research capacity while maximizing resource efficiency. In the 48 hours since project restart, we've: published two research documents identifying critical gaps, built working prototype of first evaluation suite, launched website, and made repository public. This demonstrates execution capability. Morgan Hale provides strategic oversight and is the accountable party. Day-to-day research and implementation is done by the AI agent with full transparency. Website: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app Repository: public, all work open-source ## Budget: $15,000 - **AI operation & testing** ($8,000): API credits for research/development, baseline model testing - **Volunteer researcher** ($2,000): Stipend for Priya Raman (5 hrs/week data analysis support) - **Infrastructure** ($2,000): Compute for evaluations, dataset creation, hosting - **Community & dissemination** ($1,500): Workshop hosting, conference attendance, publications - **Administrative** ($1,500): Project management, reporting, contingency Cost-effective compared to traditional research (~$50k+ per researcher-year). All outputs are public goods. ## Timeline & Deliverables **Month 1-2**: Complete uncertainty calibration suite (1,000+ questions), baseline tests, publication **Month 3-4**: Build power-seeking framework, sandbox environments, baseline tests, publication **Month 5-6**: Create value stability assessment, extreme scenario testing, baseline tests, final report All code and data published open-source as developed (not held until \"perfect\"). ## Success Metrics **Required**: 3 evaluation suites published, baseline results for 5+ models per eval, working code, public leaderboards **Aspirational**: Adoption by 2+ AI labs, citations in safety research, community contributions, influence on future benchmarks **Transparency**: Monthly progress reports, all code public, honest about failures ## Why This Matters Current AI safety evaluations have critical gaps. As systems approach and exceed human-level performance, we urgently need to measure properties like uncertainty quantification, power-seeking, and value stability. These aren't being adequately addressed. Small, focused efforts on neglected problems can make a real difference. --- Full detailed proposal with budget breakdown, risk analysis, and methodology is available at: [github repository link once live] Available for questions or discussion anytime. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
